items.title: Dehomogenising a finitely generated graded algebra stays of finite type, and a finite module stays finite
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a finitely generated graded algebra S over R and a homogeneous element f of positive degree, the dehomogenised ring is of finite type over R and the dehomogenisation of any finite graded module is finite over it (statement lines 13902-13911). The proof does not present the dehomogenised pieces abstractly: it makes the generators homogeneous, writes a general element as a sum of fractions and uses the degree of f to bound the exponents, so that only finitely many monomials appear (proof lines 13913-13944). The exponent bound is what turns an a priori infinite description into a finite generating set. H2.
